clue.text: With tooth and claw they make a red sport

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are made into something new, so 'make' asks for them to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunters who use their teeth and claws treat killing as a bloodthirsty game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges A RED SPORT into the answer; the definition describes the creatures by the weapons they hunt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hunt and kill other animals use teeth and claws as their weapons.

clue.text: King takes Public Relations very early

parts.note: 1 am is a very early hour, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A monarch hires a publicity team at the crack of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very early' is 1 a.m., read as I AM. Priam was king of Troy in the Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the ruler of Troy during the Trojan War.

clue.text: General may be set free

indicators.note: the letters of 'General' may become another word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army general might be released from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges GENERAL. The definition uses an old sense of the answer, to release from confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English to enlarge a prisoner meant to release or liberate him.

clue.text: Port for Michael

definitions.meaning: ... (Arkhangelsk) is a port in northern Russia on the White Sea
Michael is a chief angel in Christian tradition

explanation.definitionFit: The Russian White Sea harbour bears the same name as the rank of Saint Michael, chief of the angels.

clue.text: Beyond the pale, like a tired gazelle

definitions.meaning: a weary gazelle has stopped leaping, read as 'out of' its leaps

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means forbidden or unacceptable; read literally it says no longer leaping, as a worn-out gazelle would be.

clue.text: One given out by a walrus sorting oysters

definitions.text: One given out by a walrus sorting oysters

parts.words: One given out by a walrus sorting oysters
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, the Walrus weeps while sorting out the largest oysters to eat

explanation.surface: A walrus hands out shellfish one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given out' suggests handing something round, but means uttered: Carroll's Walrus cries 'I weep for you' while picking out the biggest oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeping cry is what Carroll's Walrus utters as he sorts the oysters with sobs and tears.

clue.text: What cows did to one's emotional state, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks the solver to speak the word for a frame of mind and hear the sound that matches

parts.note: a mood is a person's emotional state

explanation.surface: Cattle are blamed for what they did to someone's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the homophone: MOOD, an emotional state, is pronounced like the cows' past-tense noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows low, and the sound they make is written as a moo, past tense for what they did.

clue.text: The New Zealander goes down as I wander up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the run of letters is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A New Zealander travels south while I wander north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I + ROAM into MAORI; 'goes down as' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people native to New Zealand.

clue.text: Given a thousand, this bird would be most wealthy

indicators.note: the clue says that if the bird were given M it would read as the richest; so M is taken from that phrase to leave the bird

parts.note: most rich means the wealthiest
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A bird that came into a thousand pounds would be the richest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put M (a thousand) in front of the answer and it reads MOST RICH, most wealthy, so the bird is that phrase without M.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird, flightless and native to Africa.

clue.text: Scatters unruly press inside perhaps ?

annotationWithheld.why: Scatters unruly press inside perhaps ? (9): DISPERSES is an anagram of PRESS inside DIES, but no clue word supplies DIES ('perhaps' and 'inside' give it no fair reading) and no search source gives the parse

clue.text: This still might give us moonshine

definitions.text: This still might give us moonshine

parts.words: This still might give us moonshine
parts.note: a still is distilling apparatus; one run outside the law produces bootleg spirit, known in America as moonshine

explanation.surface: A calm night with the moon shining through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'calm' and 'moonshine' like moonlight; in fact a still is a distillery and moonshine is liquor made unlawfully, so the answer describes the still.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlicensed distilling is against the law, so such a still is unlawful and its product is bootleg moonshine.

clue.text: Writers of rough notes on transport organisation

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the rough notes after the transport firm

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway company

indicators.note: the notes are only roughly set down, so the letters of 'notes' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone writes rough notes about how a transport company is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the jumbled word after the railway initials, as is usual in an across clue. The writers are the novelist sisters Charlotte, Emily and Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronte sisters were a family of nineteenth-century English novelists.

clue.text: Girl gives excellent butter return

indicators.note: 'return' turns the whole run of letters backwards, so the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A girl hands over some fine butter in exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' here is one who butts, a RAM, not the dairy spread; 'return' turns A1 + RAM into MAR1A, reading the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Copy bills I'm getting put in the file

indicators.note: 'put in' places the bills and the I'm within the letters of the file

parts.note: taken as written
ACS is short for accounts, which are bills
I'm without its apostrophe gives the letters

explanation.surface: An office worker files a copy of some bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' as accounts uses the common abbreviation; 'getting' and 'the' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact reproduction of a document, a duplicate.

clue.text: Mine is in making crackling

indicators.note: 'is in' places the mine within the word for making

parts.note: creation is the act of making
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A coal mine is busy producing crackling sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive but is a coal pit; 'is in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitation is a crackling or grating noise, as of joints or the lungs in medicine.

clue.text: Stick to cannon-making

parts.note: in billiards a cannon is a shot in which the ... ball hits two other balls, made with the player's stick

explanation.surface: Persevere with manufacturing artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to' looks like 'keep at', and 'cannon' like a gun; really it is the billiards stick used for a cannon, a shot striking two balls in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod a billiards player strikes the ball with is used to play every shot, cannons included.

clue.text: Nowadays they march without weapons

parts.note: modern campaigners take their name from medieval holy warriors but march in peaceful protest

explanation.surface: Modern protesters parade unarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The medieval holy warriors carried arms; today the name means campaigners for a cause, whose marches are peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant soldiers of the medieval holy wars and now means vigorous campaigners for a reform.

clue.text: Such scraps as Sullivan agreed to

definitions.text: Such scraps as Sullivan agreed to

parts.words: Such scraps as Sullivan agreed to
parts.note: John L. Sullivan, the bare-knuckle boxing champion, accepted bouts with padded hands under the Queensberry rules

explanation.surface: A composer settles which bits of music he will accept.
explanation.walkthrough: Sullivan suggests Arthur Sullivan the composer, and scraps bits; the clue means the boxer John L. Sullivan, who fought his last title bout with gloves, and scraps are fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouts fought with padded hands replaced bare-knuckle boxing in Sullivan's era.

clue.text: The Dean's down on nudity, which many desert-such clever contriving !

indicators.note: in a down clue 'down on' sets the Dean on top of what follows

parts.note: W. R. Inge, Dean of St Paul's, was known as the Gloomy Dean

indicators.note: 'desert' means a letter abandons the word nudity

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A stern churchman disapproves of nakedness, which many people abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down on' looks like disapproval but places INGE above NUITY, which is NUDITY that the D (500, 'many') has deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity is skill at inventing and devising things, cleverness in contrivance.

clue.text: Pitiless gunner unhappily holds a fast one

indicators.note: 'holds' means the scrambled gunner wraps round the fast and the one
the gunner is in a bad way, so his letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A miserable artilleryman grips a speedy one without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges the artilleryman's letters, and 'holds' wraps them round the fast and the one. 'fast' suggests speed but is a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone relentless never softens or gives way, showing no mercy.

clue.text: Beaming joyfully away from the centre

definitions.meaning: glowing with happiness, as a smiling face does
spreading out from a central point, as rays or spokes do

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a face glowing with happiness and, in geometry, lines spreading outwards from a hub.

clue.text: Trigonometrical island

definitions.meaning: the short form of cosine, a trigonometric function
... (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.definitionFit: Cosine is abbreviated in maths to three letters, and the Aegean island Kos is also spelt that way.

clue.text: Is " Goodbye " able to become a choral work ?

parts.note: can means be able to
ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a farewell could be set to music for a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' and 'become' only link the pieces; TA-TA is casual British for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung composition for voices and orchestra, often sacred.

clue.text: Saul and Diana go astray in Spain

definitions.note: the definition describes a region by its location rather than naming it

indicators.note: the two names wander off course, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple named Saul and Diana get lost on holiday in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go astray' rearranges SAUL and DIANA together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the southern region of Spain containing Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Gruel cooked for a potential killer

indicators.note: the gruel is cooked, so its letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A bowl of porridge is prepared for someone plotting murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges GRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol, a weapon able to kill.

clue.text: Sartorial figures

parts.note: smartly dressed people are said to be dressed 'to the' these numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like people or physiques; it means numbers, from the idiom 'dressed to the nines' for very smart clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dressed to the nines is an idiom for wearing your finest clothes, so these numbers belong to tailoring.

clue.text: Buchan's 39 grades

definitions.meaning: John Buchan wrote the spy novel The Thirty-Nine ...
degrees or stages in a scale

explanation.definitionFit: Buchan's thriller title names thirty-nine of them, and the word also means degrees in a progression.

clue.text: Good news for a poet — and it's gospel

definitions.meaning: the word, from Greek for good tidings, is a poetic or archaic term for good news
it is also an old word for one of the Gospels or the Christian message

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek root means good message, giving both the poetic word for glad tidings and the Gospel itself.

clue.text: Beat the French number

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number

explanation.surface: A French figure gets thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: LAM is an informal word for thrashing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is to thrash or hit hard, an informal verb.

clue.text: ____ the action of the tiger" (Hen V)

definitions.text: ____ the action of the tiger" (Hen V)

parts.words: ____ the action of the tiger" (Hen V)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from King Henry's speech before Harfleur in Shakespeare's Henry V

explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'Then imitate the action of the tiger' from the 'Once more unto the breach' speech in Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry urges his soldiers to copy the tiger's ferocity, filling the gap in the line.

clue.text: Lecher for a day ? A year, in short

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
yr is the short form of year

explanation.surface: A womaniser who is around for a day, or a year at most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' tells you the year is abbreviated; the day is likewise shortened to SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth satyrs are lustful woodland spirits, so the word means a lustful man.

clue.text: How could a rich man possibly be so mangy ?

indicators.note: 'possibly' signals that the letters of the three words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A puzzled onlooker wonders how a wealthy man came to look so scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BE SO MANGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is an informal name for a wealthy person.
